title: Code Review with AI
description: Use AI to catch bugs, improve code quality, and enforce standards before human reviewers even look at your PR.

data.text: What AI Can and Cannot Review

AI is excellent at catching mechanical issues: style violations, missing error handling, potential null dereferences, and deviations from project patterns. It is not good at evaluating whether the code actually solves the right problem, whether the architecture is sound, or whether the feature matches the product requirements. Think of AI review as a first-pass quality check, not a replacement for human review.

The simplest way to use AI for code review is to paste your diff into a chat interface before opening a PR. Ask the AI to review the changes, point out issues, and suggest improvements. This pre-commit review catches problems that would otherwise waste your human reviewer's time.

data.title: Review the diff, not the whole file
data.text: Paste only the changed code (the diff) into the AI review prompt, not the entire file. The AI only needs to see what you changed, not the 500 lines you did not touch. Use git diff to generate the diff and paste that.

data.title: Every AI review prompt should include:
items: The project's language, framework, and conventions
Specific concerns: 'Focus on security, error handling, and performance'
Context: what the PR is trying to accomplish

data.title: AI is strong at detecting:
items: Missing null checks or unhandled edge cases
Hardcoded values that should be constants
Missing error handling in async operations

data.title: AI review has blind spots:
items: Whether the feature actually meets the product requirements
Whether the architecture is appropriate for the long term
Business logic errors that look correct syntactically
Performance issues that only manifest at scale
Whether the change breaks something in a different module
Whether the commit message accurately describes the changes

data.text: Using AI for PR Description Generation

AI can also help write better PR descriptions. Paste your diff and ask: 'Write a PR description for this change. Include a summary of what changed, why, and any testing considerations.' This produces clearer, more consistent PR descriptions and saves time writing them by hand.

data.title: AI review prompt
data.content: "Please review this PR diff. The change adds a discount code feature to the checkout flow. Focus on: security (input validation, SQL injection), error handling (what happens when the discount code is invalid or expired), and consistency with our existing patterns in src/checkout/. Flag any issues and suggest improvements."
data.code:
AI review prompt:

"Please review this PR diff. The change adds a discount code feature to the checkout flow. Focus on:
- Security (input validation, SQL injection)
- Error handling (what happens when the discount code is invalid or expired)
- Consistency with our existing patterns in `src/checkout/`

Flag any issues and suggest improvements."

data.text: GitHub Copilot can review PRs directly through the GitHub interface. When a PR is opened, Copilot can automatically comment on potential issues in the changed code. This is not a replacement for human review but provides an additional layer of automated checking that runs as soon as the PR is opened.

When AI flags an issue, evaluate it before acting. Not every AI suggestion is correct, but most are worth considering. If the AI points out a real issue, fix it and move on. If it is wrong, ignore it. Over time, you will develop a sense for which types of AI feedback to trust.

data.title: Human review is still required
data.text: AI review is a pre-filter, not a replacement. The final code review must still be done by a human who understands the business context, the product requirements, and the team's standards. AI catches mechanical issues; humans catch architectural and business issues.

data.title: AI code review
points: Review the diff, not the whole file
AI catches mechanical issues: style, null checks, security patterns
AI misses business logic and architectural problems
Use AI to generate PR descriptions and review comments
Always require human review before merging
